auditLimits.pageLevelScan: All 365 daily 2026 records using the live Divinum Officium 1954 Mass iCalendar endpoint, with targeted Mass-page checks for source occurrence semantics
auditLimits.remaining: Other years and full primary-source page collation remain open; this audit does not claim that the entire profile is page-perfect.
knownSourceAnomalies: 2026-02-16: Restore the 54 displays Credo for the feria, while the primary Divinum Officium Quad5-1 Mass record has no Credo rule; the profile follows the primary record.

2026-03-08: Restore the 54 displays Gloria and no Credo for the Third Sunday of Lent, while the primary Divinum Officium Quad3-0 record has no Gloria and Credo; the profile follows the primary record.
unsupportedData: Individual primary-source page numbers are not encoded; the annual scan used machine-readable Ordo records and did not collate Missale page references.

decisions: pre-55 grade is explicit; no 1962 class attribute is emitted
BLUE is normalized to pre-1955 WHITE; five-color plus rose vocabulary only
every entry carries explicit transfer, octave, vigil, Mass, and reading metadata
sourceRank retains DO decimal precedence so intermediate values are not lost
temporal sunday_rules carry the complete Advent, Epiphany, and post-Pentecost Sunday propers with Easter offsets where applicable
octave metadata is attached only to source-confirmed octave members; Mass-only or Vespers-only octave references remain non-commemorated at Mass
all octave-bearing entries carry explicit nameResId keys in each of the seven locale dictionaries, with ordinal placeholders checked
the movable Patronage octave days are generic commemoration records; the 2026 St. Mark conflict is an explicit direct-Mass omission
major Advent/Lenten ferias outrank Simplex feasts when the source orders the feria as the Mass
direct Mass-page occurrence labels override Office-level iCalendar descriptions when the two differ
Brazilian propers are stored in a separate 1954 local asset; an explicit local rank replaces a universal record with the same observance identity.
Sunday common vigils are suppressed at Mass except for the explicit transferred Vigil of St. Thomas

rules: Saint Joseph uses SaintJoseph for the March 19 feast and the movable Patronage feast and octave; other Joseph saints use Common.
B.V.M. proper and octave entries use BlessedVirginMary; unrelated female saints use Common.
St John the Baptist feast and common octave use Common, matching the checked 2026 Ordo records.
Holy Cross, Precious Blood, All Souls, and church dedications use their proper prefaces.
Septuagesima Sundays use Trinity; the Epiphany vigil uses Christmas; Good Friday has no preface; Ascension vigil uses Easter.

unresolvedEvidenceGaps: The generated normalized XML has been contract-validated and cross-checked against the DO 1939/1954 machine-readable inputs and PRE55_RULES.md. A page-by-page comparison of every reading against the 1954 scan remains for the phase-6 verification matrix.
